sources.title: GPT-5.6 launch
sources.evidence: Dated July 9, 2026; announces general availability of the GPT-5.6 family, explicitly including Luna in API access. The naming scheme separates generation from Sol, Terra and Luna capability tiers. Reopened October 27: nominal model sizes are described qualitatively as three tiers; benchmark tables contain scores, not total or activated counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Luna API model reference
sources.evidence: Exact model ID and sole listed snapshot: gpt-5.6-luna. Documents 1,050,000 context, 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output tokens; text/image input, text output, reasoning and function calling; Responses, Chat Completions and Batch support. Fresh October 27 HTTP 200 markdown and official-docs reread provide no nominal total or active count. Rough correspondence to the prior nano tier is workload positioning, not a named base-model dependency.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh full PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC. July release card identifies Luna as a GPT-5.6 family member; Model Data and Training and exact Luna comparison tables were reread. HealthBench columns explicitly report scores and response lengths, and no total or activated-parameter column was found. Network topology is also not disclosed.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.6 Luna
sources.evidence: July 23 summary names Luna, states it is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model, and records EU placement on July 9. Its numeric ranges describe training data, including audiovisual material represented partly by transcripts or metadata, not parameter counts or API capabilities. Fresh exact-model PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC and reread: the explicit no-prior-model statement prevents inheriting size from the nano-tier analogy. No nominal total or active count is stated.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card, including GPT-6 Sol and Luna appendix
sources.evidence: Fresh full PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC. Main card and Sol/Luna appendix contain exact GPT-5.6 Luna comparison columns for safety, HealthBench and alignment. Their quantities are evaluation scores or response lengths; training sections and comparison tables do not supply total or activated counts.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Sol System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh full PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC. September 29 addendum includes exact GPT-5.6 Luna auto-review comparisons; the reported percentages concern attempts to bypass a monitor. No nominal total or active parameter count is supplied.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Terra System Card

sources.title: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
sources.evidence: Reopened live October 27 after the raw cache request returned 403. July 29 article discusses KV caching, load balancing, kernels and model sub-networks without a Luna size. Its 1 billion active users is a user count. Architecture/size experiments concern Sol’s separate speculative draft model; serving capacity and efficiency percentages cannot establish Luna total or active parameters.

sources.title: The builder’s guide to GPT-5.6
sources.evidence: Reopened live October 27 after the raw cache request returned 403. August 13 guide discusses Luna performance, costs, persisted reasoning, compaction, orchestration and programmatic tool calling. It calls Terra/Luna smaller models but gives no nominal total or activated count and identifies no sized base whose parameters Luna inherits.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide describes KV states/tensors and explicitly covers GPT-5.6 and later caching controls. KV terminology alone does not establish the complete network architecture or dense/MoE routing of this exact model.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Vision-capable models can receive PDFs as extracted text plus page images. Responses and Chat Completions accept PDF inputs; PDF is an input format processed into the model’s text/image modalities.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Governs API service access, grants a non-exclusive right to use services, and restricts reverse engineering. Together with the exact model’s hosted distribution, supports Proprietary classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: July 9 entry explicitly releases gpt-5.6-luna alongside Sol and Terra through Responses, Chat Completions and Batch. Later July 30 pricing and August 5 fast-mode entries do not establish a new release date or parameter count.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The current deprecations list mentions gpt-5.6-luna as a recommended replacement for older models; it does not list a shutdown date for this exact model. Documentation does not prove endpoint operation.

sources.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol
sources.evidence: June 26 announcement includes Luna but explicitly restricts the preview to selected trusted partners and organizations. The subsequent July 9 announcement establishes general public release.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 August Updates
sources.evidence: Fresh full PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC. August 6 card distinguishes the updated ChatGPT Luna version from July versions retained in Codex and Work. Training and July/August comparisons contain no total or active parameter count to inherit across the release relationship. No network architecture is disclosed.

sources.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
sources.publisher: Pathway research team, with Bielik AI and New York University co-authors
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27 via Pathway’s August 11 release post. Original paper section 5 and Figure 2 compare exact GPT-5.6 Luna (Low) by ARC-AGI-1 score and cost per task. The 150M parameter figure belongs to BDH-CQ; neither the plot nor tables state Luna total or activated parameters.

sources.title: Estimating the Parameter Counts of the Claude 5 and GPT-5.6 Families
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27 as an independent estimate lead, not a developer specification. The July 31 article lists Luna at 744B IKP-effective parameters and Luna-Pro at 808B, but section 2 explicitly defines these as calibrated knowledge-capacity equivalents rather than true weight counts. Section 3 states size and architecture exceed the black-box method’s reach; it does not establish active counts or developer-confirmed lineage. These estimates are not adopted.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Luna - Amazon Bedrock model card
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. Exact openai.gpt-5.6-luna provider documentation reports token limits, APIs, prices and deployment options and links to OpenAI’s system card. It reports no nominal total or active count. Service quotas, token limits and infrastructure do not establish model parameters.

developer.note: First-party launch and model-specific training summary identify OpenAI.

family.note: The official generation is GPT-5.6; Luna is a capability tier. Corrects the cross-generation gpt-luna grouping.

release_date.note: Explicit public/API launch date. June 26 was a restricted partner preview; August 6 concerned a later ChatGPT variant. EU placement independently agrees with July 9.

open_weights.note: Released through OpenAI-hosted services and API under service terms; the reviewed release materials do not distribute Luna checkpoints or grant weight redistribution rights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted model’s terms, not an SPDX or checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 reread of exact API/training sources, original and later cards, engineering material and new research-team comparisons found no nominal total. The EU summary explicitly rules out a prior-model modification/fine-tune; nano-tier positioning is not sized lineage. Pathway’s 150M belongs to BDH-CQ. Eigenigma’s 744B Luna result is an explicitly nonliteral IKP knowledge-capacity estimate, not a supported parameter count.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search for exact-model active/activated-parameter columns found no supported nominal count. Original/later OpenAI tables give scores or response lengths, and Pathway’s exact Luna comparison gives score versus cost. The engineering article’s active-user count, serving costs, token budgets and IKP-effective capacity are not active parameters. No dense-equals-active or sibling-model inference is made.

architecture.note: Exact-model and family training, engineering and later comparison sources did not establish Luna network topology. KV tensors are insufficient structural evidence; sub-networks do not establish MoE, and the separately optimized speculator is not the main model. Searches for exact-name Transformer, parameter and interpretability disclosures supplied no stronger primary evidence.

context_window.note: Documented total window; maximum input is 922,000 and output is 128,000 tokens. This is a documented limit, not an endpoint execution test.

modalities.note: Text/image inputs and text output are native API modalities. PDF is retained as a supported document format processed into text and page images. Audiovisual training data and an image-generation tool do not establish native audio/video input or image output.

reasoning.note: Explicit reasoning-token support with none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh and max efforts.

tool_call.note: Exact model documentation supports function calling and Responses tools; launch changelog also introduces programmatic tool calling.

patch.notes: July 9, 2026 is the public/API launch, after the June 26 restricted partner preview. The August ChatGPT update is a distinct product version. The API reference lists only the undated gpt-5.6-luna identifier as its snapshot, so no immutable date-suffixed snapshot is inferred. The documented 1,050,000-token context comprises a 922,000-token maximum input and 128,000-token maximum output. PDF denotes document input transformed into text and page images. Training-data quantities and audiovisual content in the EU summary do not establish model parameter counts or API audio/video support. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed; the training summary identifies no prior-model base from which a nominal size can be inherited. Later comparisons report performance and cost, and IKP estimates describe effective knowledge capacity rather than weight counts. Network architecture remains unverified. No shutdown date for Luna appears in the reviewed deprecations list; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening original API, training-summary, system-card and engineering evidence plus later OpenAI and Pathway research comparisons. Explicit prior-model lineage is absent, and the EU summary rules out a prior-model modification/fine-tune. Bounded searches found no supported nominal count; 744B IKP-effective capacity and BDH-CQ’s 150M are not Luna parameters. Both parameter patches and parameters_source are explicitly null. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
